s: Who were Vipravinodulu during the Vijayanagara period?
o: They are a caste of Shudras who depend only on Brahmins for their sustenance.
Shudras performing their arts to entertain Brahmins.
Brahmin jugglers who entertain only Brahmins in their homes.
Brahmin scholars skilled in all arts.
x:
During the Vijayanagara period, Vipravinodulu were Brahmin performers and jugglers who entertained members of the Brahmin community through various magical tricks, acrobatics and amusing performances. The term literally means "those who entertain Brahmins." They formed a distinct professional group and are mentioned in literary works and historical records describing the social life of the Vijayanagara Empire. Their performances were generally confined to Brahmin households and religious gatherings. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Vipravinodulu – Brahmin Jugglers
• Period – Vijayanagara

x: Brahmin jugglers, who provided indoor entertainment to brahmins only Vipra-Vinodins were Brahmin jugglers who provided indoor entertainment exclusively to fellow Brahmins. This reflects the caste-segregated nature of certain entertainment traditions in the Vijayanagara period. Such specialised entertainer groups are noted in period literature and inscriptions.

s:
According to Portuguese writer Nuniz, the women in Vijayanagara Empire were experts in which of the following areas?
1. Wrestling
2. Astrology
3. Accounting
4. Soothsaying
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All are correct: The Vijayanagara Empire was ruled by four successive dynasties: the Sangama (c. 1336–1485 CE), Saluva (c. 1485–1503 CE), Tuluva (c. 1503–1570 CE), and Aravidu dynasties, the last continuing till the end of the 17th century. A significant understanding of the empire's history comes from the accounts of two Portuguese Medieval Indian History PMF IAS IH – 41 chroniclers, Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz. Writing in the sixteenth century, their narratives provide valuable first-hand insights. Domingo Paes recorded his observations during 1520–22, in the reign of Krishnadevaraya, while Fernao Nuniz wrote around 1535–37, during the rule of Achyuta Deva Raya. Both rulers were key figures of the Tuluva dynasty. Women in Vijayanagara society enjoyed a notable status and actively participated in political, social, and cultural life. They were engaged in activities such as wrestling, swordsmanship, the use of shields, music, and other fine arts, and some also received substantial literary education. Nuniz notes that women held diverse roles, including wrestling, astrology, and soothsaying. He also notes the presence of women officials who kept expense records in the palace and documented administrative affairs, often cross-checking these records with those kept by external scribes.

s: Which inscription contains the 12 Sutras to be followed during the construction of Tataka?
x:
The Porumamilla Inscription is an important historical source that records twelve engineering principles (Dwadasha Sutras) to be followed during the construction of tanks (Tataka). These guidelines relate to the selection of suitable sites, strength of bunds, water storage capacity, sluices and maintenance. The inscription demonstrates the advanced knowledge of irrigation engineering that existed in medieval Andhra. It is one of the most frequently asked inscriptions in APPSC examinations. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Inscription – Porumamilla
• Importance – Twelve Sutras of Tank Construction

s: The rules to be followed in the construction of Tataka are mentioned in?
x:
The Porumamilla Inscription contains the famous Twelve Principles (Dwadasha Sutras) to be followed while constructing a Tataka (tank/reservoir). These principles deal with the selection of site, embankment construction, water storage, maintenance and irrigation management. The inscription reflects the advanced engineering knowledge of medieval Andhra and the importance given to irrigation. It is one of the most frequently asked topics in APPSC examinations. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Inscription – Porumamilla
• Importance – Twelve Principles for Tank Construction

In the entertainments of the Vijayanagara kings, apart from Yakshaganam, which art form entertained the common rural people of Andhra?
x:
During the Vijayanagara period, several traditional performing arts flourished under royal patronage. While Yakshaganam was popular in royal courts and among elite audiences, the Leather Puppet Dance (Tholu Bommalata) was the most popular entertainment among the rural population. Tholu Bommalata is a traditional shadow puppet theatre in which colourful leather puppets are manipulated behind a white screen with the help of light. Stories from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas were presented through music, narration and dialogue. This art form served not only as entertainment but also as a medium for religious instruction and moral education. Andhra Pradesh continues to be one of the most important centres of Tholu Bommalata. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Traditional Shadow Puppet Theatre – Tholu Bommalata
• Popular during – Vijayanagara Period
• Themes – Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas
